records.source: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו אַתָּ֤ה זָקַ֨נְתָּה֙ בָּ֣אתָ בַיָּמִ֔ים וְהָאָ֛רֶץ נִשְׁאֲרָ֥ה הַרְבֵּֽה־מְאֹ֖ד לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And Joshua [was] old, advanced in the days; and said Yahweh to him, You [are] old, you have advanced in the days, and the land remains very much to possess it.
pieces: Joshua had now grown old, far along in years. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You have grown old and are far along in years, and very much of the land still remains to be taken.

L.1: And Joshua was old, advanced in days. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You are old, you have advanced in days, and very much of the land remains to possess.

R.1: Joshua had grown old. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You have become an old man, and there is still a lot of land left for Israel to take.

decisions.choice: old, advanced in days: very old, near the end of a long life
decisions.reason: "Coming into the days" is a set way of saying a person has lived many years (Genesis 24:1, of Abraham; 1 Kings 1:1, of David). The same words come back when Joshua gives his last speeches (23:1-2). He dies at 110 (24:29).

decisions.choice: the land remains to possess: the conquest is not complete
decisions.reason: The summary in 11:23 said Joshua took the whole land. Here the LORD says much is still left. Both are true in their way: the power of the kings was broken, but many regions and towns were still held by their peoples. Verses 2-6 list them, and verse 6 promises that the LORD himself will drive them out.

decisions.choice: to possess it: to take it over and hold it
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession of land, which often meant driving out those who held it. The task left to Israel is to occupy what the LORD gives.

decisions.choice: left for Israel to take
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel as the people who are to take the land; the Hebrew leaves the subject unstated, but the rest of the speech makes it plain (verse 6).

records.heading: Very much of the land still remains

records.source: זֹ֥את הָאָ֖רֶץ הַנִּשְׁאָ֑רֶת כָּל־גְּלִיל֥וֹת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וְכָל־הַגְּשׁוּרִֽי׃
records.gloss: This [is] the land the remaining: all [the] regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurite[s],
pieces: This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the land of the Geshurites,

L.2: This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

R.2: This is the land that is still left: all the land of the Philistines and of the Geshurites.

decisions.choice: regions: districts or areas
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "circle" or "round", and names a district (it is used of the districts of the Jordan, 22:10-11). Here it names the lands held by the Philistines along the southern coast.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites: a people in the far south, not the Geshur of verse 11
decisions.reason: These Geshurites are named with the Philistines and lived south of them, toward Egypt; David raided them from Ziklag (1 Samuel 27:8). They are a different people from the Geshurites north-east of the Jordan in verses 11 and 13.

decisions.choice: the land of the Geshurites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the land of" the Geshurites, so that the list stays a list of regions, as the Hebrew means.

records.source: מִֽן־הַשִּׁיח֞וֹר אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מִצְרַ֗יִם וְעַ֨ד גְּב֤וּל עֶקְרוֹן֙ צָפ֔וֹנָה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י תֵּחָשֵׁ֑ב חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת׀סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים הָעַזָּתִ֤י וְהָאַשְׁדּוֹדִי֙ הָאֶשְׁקְלוֹנִ֣י הַגִּתִּ֔י וְהָעֶקְרוֹנִ֖י וְהָעַוִּֽים׃
records.gloss: from the Shihor which [is] on [the] face of Egypt and to [the] border of Ekron northward, to the Canaanite it is reckoned; five rulers of [the] Philistines, the Gazite and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim,
pieces: from the Shihor east of Egypt as far north as the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite land. There are the five rulers of the Philistines, those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and there are the Avvim,

L.3: from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, and as far as the border of Ekron northward, it is counted as Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, the Gazite and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim,

R.3: It runs from the Shihor stream, east of Egypt, north to the border of Ekron. All of this counts as part of the land of Canaan. There are the five Philistine rulers, of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron. There are also the Avvim.

decisions.choice: the Shihor east of Egypt: a stream on Egypt's border
decisions.reason: The name means "the black (waters)". In Isaiah 23:3 and Jeremiah 2:18 it names a branch of the Nile. Here it marks the south-western edge of the land, and it may be the same as "the Wadi of Egypt", the dry stream bed that formed the southern border (15:4, 47; Numbers 34:5). "On the face of" Egypt means facing it, to the east.

decisions.choice: counted as Canaanite: part of the promised land, though the Philistines held it
decisions.reason: The coastal strip from the Shihor to Ekron was in Philistine hands, but it is reckoned as part of Canaan, the land promised to Israel (Genesis 15:18-21; Numbers 34:2-5). It is therefore among the land still left to take.

decisions.choice: the five rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: The word for "rulers" is used only of the Philistine leaders. Each of the five main cities, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, had its own ruler, and they acted together (Judges 16:5; 1 Samuel 6:16-18). The Hebrew names the rulers by their peoples: "the Gazite", "the Ashdodite" and so on.

decisions.choice: the Avvim: an older people of the coast near Gaza
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 2:23 says the Avvim lived in villages as far as Gaza before the people from Caphtor, the Philistines, destroyed them and settled in their place.

decisions.choice: those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the city names instead of "the Gazite, the Ashdodite" and so on, which in English sound like single persons. Literal keeps the form of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the Shihor stream; counts as part of the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable adds "stream" so the reader knows the Shihor is water, and makes plain that "Canaanite" means the land of Canaan that God promised. It splits the long list into short sentences.

records.source: מִתֵּימָ֞ן כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י וּמְעָרָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַצִּידֹנִ֖ים עַד־אֲפֵ֑קָה עַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃
records.gloss: from [the] south, all [the] land of the Canaanite, and Mearah which [belongs] to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to [the] border of the Amorite;
pieces: from the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the border of the Amorites;

L.4: from [the] south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;

R.4: From the south there is all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the people of Sidon, as far as Aphek and the border of the Amorites.

decisions.choice: from the south: read with the verse that follows it, or as a note on where the Avvim lived
alternatives: the Avvim in the south; all the land of the Canaanites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verse division separates "from the south" from the Avvim at the end of verse 3, and opens the next part of the list with it: the Canaanite land along the coast, from the south up to the land of Sidon. But the words can also be read with the Avvim, "the Avvim in the south", since they lived near Gaza (Deuteronomy 2:23). The sense of the whole is the same either way: the coastal lands from south to north are still to be taken.

decisions.choice: Mearah: a place name
alternatives: the cave that belongs to the Sidonians
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for "cave", and it may be read "and the cave that belongs to the Sidonians". As a name it is otherwise unknown. Either way it is a place in the land of Sidon, on the northern coast.

decisions.choice: the Sidonians; Aphek; the border of the Amorites: the far north
decisions.reason: The Sidonians were the people of the coastal cities around Sidon, in what is now Lebanon. This Aphek is a northern town, not the Aphek of 12:18 in the coastal plain. The Amorites here are the peoples of the land of Amurru in Syria, north of Lebanon, so the list reaches the northern limit of the promised land.

decisions.choice: the people of Sidon
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Sidon" for "the Sidonians".

records.source: וְהָאָ֣רֶץ הַגִּבְלִ֗י וְכָל־הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ מִזְרַ֣ח הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ מִבַּ֣עַל גָּ֔ד תַּ֖חַת הַר־חֶרְמ֑וֹן עַ֖ד לְב֥וֹא חֲמָֽת׃
records.gloss: and the land of the Gebalite, and all the Lebanon [toward the] rising of the sun, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;
pieces: and the land of the Gebalites, and the whole of Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;

L.5: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;

R.5: There is the land of the people of Gebal, and all the Lebanon mountains to the east, from Baal-gad at the foot of Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.

decisions.choice: the Gebalites: the people of Gebal on the coast north of Sidon
decisions.reason: Gebal is the old Phoenician port later known as Byblos, north of modern Beirut (Ezekiel 27:9). Its land marks the northern part of the coast.

decisions.choice: all Lebanon toward the sunrise: the mountain country east of the coast
decisions.reason: The Lebanon here is the range of mountains inland from the coastal cities, together with the valley between it and the Hermon range. "Toward the rising of the sun" places it east of the land of Gebal.

decisions.choice: from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath: the northern limits
decisions.reason: Baal-gad lay at the foot of Hermon and marks the northern end of Joshua's conquest (11:17; 12:7). Lebo-hamath, "the entrance to Hamath", was on the way north toward Hamath in Syria and marks the northern border of the promised land (Numbers 34:8).

decisions.choice: the Lebanon mountains
decisions.reason: Readable adds "mountains" so the reader knows Lebanon here is a mountain range, not the modern country.

records.source: כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָ֠הָר מִֽן־הַלְּבָנ֞וֹן עַד־מִשְׂרְפֹ֥ת מַ֨יִם֙ כָּל־צִ֣ידֹנִ֔ים אָֽנֹכִי֙ אוֹרִישֵׁ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֠ק הַפִּלֶ֤הָ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּֽנַחֲלָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוִּיתִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: all [the] inhabitants of the hill country from the Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all [the] Sidonians, I will dispossess them from before [the] sons of Israel; only allot it to Israel as an inheritance as I have commanded you.
pieces: all who live in the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I am the one who will drive them out before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Only allot the land to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.

L.6: all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will dispossess them from before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.

R.6: All the people of the hill country, from the Lebanon mountains to Misrephoth-maim, all the people of Sidon: I myself will drive them out of the way of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. You must divide the land among the Israelites by lot. It will be their own land, as I commanded you.

decisions.choice: I myself will dispossess them: the LORD will do it
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out before the verb, which stresses it. Joshua is old and cannot finish the conquest, but the land left is not lost: the LORD himself will drive out its peoples.

decisions.choice: Misrephoth-maim: a place on the coast south of Sidon
decisions.reason: The pursuit after the battle of the waters of Merom went as far as this place (11:8). The name may mean "burnings of water", perhaps from hot springs or salt works, but that is not certain.

decisions.choice: only allot it to Israel: divide it by lot now, before it is won
decisions.reason: The verb means "make it fall", that is, cast the lot (Numbers 26:55-56). Joshua is to give out even the land not yet taken, trusting the promise of the LORD. "Only" sets his task against the LORD's: the LORD drives out, Joshua allots.

decisions.choice: inheritance: land held as a lasting family possession
decisions.reason: The word names property handed down in a family. The land is given to the tribes and their clans to keep from one generation to the next (Numbers 26:52-56; 34:13).

decisions.choice: dispossess (Literal) / drive out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb used of nations means to drive them out so that others take their place. Literal keeps "dispossess"; Balanced and Readable say "drive out", as elsewhere in Joshua.

decisions.choice: divide the land ... by lot. It will be their own land
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the land is divided by lot and explains "inheritance" as land of their own, in two short sentences.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַלֵּ֞ק אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את בְּנַחֲלָ֖ה לְתִשְׁעַ֣ת הַשְּׁבָטִ֑ים וַחֲצִ֖י הַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And now divide the land the this as an inheritance to [the] nine of the tribes and half of the tribe the Manasseh.
pieces: So now divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."

L.7: And now divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."

R.7: So now divide this land among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh, to be their own."

decisions.choice: the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh: the tribes still to receive land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Twelve tribes had a share in the land. Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh already had land east of the Jordan from Moses (verse 8; Numbers 32). Levi received no land (verse 14). The descendants of Joseph were counted as two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh (14:3-4), so nine and a half tribes remained.

decisions.choice: and now: so, in the light of this
decisions.reason: "Now" here draws the conclusion from what has been said: because the LORD will drive the peoples out, Joshua is to divide the land at once.

decisions.choice: to be their own
decisions.reason: Readable gives "as an inheritance" as "to be their own", as in verse 6.

records.source: עִמּ֗וֹ הָרֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְהַגָּדִ֔י לָקְח֖וּ נַחֲלָתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן לָהֶ֜ם מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ נָתַ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: With it the Reubenite and the Gadite received their inheritance, which gave to them Moses beyond the Jordan eastward, just as gave to them Moses [the] servant of Yahweh,
pieces: With the other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them east of the Jordan, as Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had assigned it to them,

L.8: With it the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moses gave them across the Jordan eastward, just as Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them,

R.8: The other half of the tribe of Manasseh, together with the tribes of Reuben and Gad, had already received their land on the east side of the Jordan. Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, had given it to them.

decisions.choice: with it: with the other half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: "It" must be the tribe of Manasseh named at the end of verse 7, but the half meant here is the other half, which settled east of the Jordan (verses 29-31). The sentence turns from the land still to be shared out to the land the eastern tribes already held.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text kept as it stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew passes very briefly from one half of Manasseh to the other. The ancient Greek translation has a fuller wording at the end of verse 7 and the start of verse 8 that describes the western land and then names the eastern half-tribe together with Reuben and Gad. A copyist's eye may have skipped from one mention of Manasseh to the next and left words out of the Hebrew, or the Greek may have filled out a short text. The Hebrew is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan eastward: east of the river
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" is said from the viewpoint of the land west of the river; "eastward" makes the side plain, as in 1:15.

decisions.choice: Moses the servant of the LORD: his title, as in 1:1
decisions.reason: The title marks Moses as the one who belonged to God and acted for him. The eastern tribes' land rests on his grant (Numbers 32:33; Deuteronomy 3:12-17), and Joshua does not change it.

decisions.choice: the other half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the half-tribe that "it" refers to, because "with it" alone would point back to the half-tribe of verse 7, which received land west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

records.gloss: from Aroer, which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi Arnon, and the city which [is] in [the] middle of the wadi, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon;
pieces: from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,

L.9: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the wadi, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,

R.9: Their land reached from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River valley, and the town in the middle of the valley. It took in all the high plain of Medeba as far as Dibon.

decisions.choice: Aroer on the edge of the wadi Arnon: the southern limit of the eastern lands
decisions.reason: The Arnon cuts a deep gorge through the high land east of the Dead Sea and was the border between Moab and the land Israel took from Sihon (Numbers 21:13; Deuteronomy 2:36; 3:12). Aroer stood on its northern rim.

decisions.choice: the city in the middle of the wadi: a town in the gorge, not named
decisions.reason: The same unnamed town is mentioned with Aroer in Deuteronomy 2:36 and in verse 16. It may be Ar, the Moabite town by the Arnon (Numbers 21:15), but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the plateau: the high tableland north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: The word means level ground. It names the flat upland between the Arnon and Heshbon, with towns such as Medeba and Dibon (Deuteronomy 3:10).

decisions.choice: wadi Arnon, city (Literal) / Arnon Valley, town (Balanced) / Arnon River valley, town (Readable)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that may run dry. Literal keeps "wadi"; Balanced and Readable say "valley". The word for "city" is used of any walled settlement, large or small; Balanced and Readable say "town" through these lists.

decisions.choice: Their land reached from ...
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and supplies "their land reached" for the list that verse 8 opens.

records.source: וְכֹ֗ל עָרֵי֙ סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן עַד־גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and all [the] cities of Sihon king of the Amorite, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as [the] border of [the] sons of Ammon;
pieces: and all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, up to the Ammonite border,

L.10: and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the sons of Ammon,

R.10: It took in all the towns of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon: the king Israel defeated under Moses
decisions.reason: Sihon refused Israel passage and was defeated, and his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok was taken (Numbers 21:21-31; Deuteronomy 2:24-37; Joshua 12:2).

decisions.choice: the border of the sons of Ammon: the eastern edge, toward the desert
decisions.reason: The Ammonites lived on the eastern side of Gilead, around Rabbah (verse 25). Their border was along the upper Jabbok (Deuteronomy 3:16).

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the Ammonites" for "the sons of Ammon", the name of the people. Literal keeps "the sons of Ammon".

records.source: וְהַגִּלְעָ֞ד וּגְב֧וּל הַגְּשׁוּרִ֣י וְהַמַּעֲכָתִ֗י וְכֹ֨ל הַ֥ר חֶרְמ֛וֹן וְכָל־הַבָּשָׁ֖ן עַד־סַלְכָֽה׃
records.gloss: and the Gilead, and [the] territory of the Geshurite and the Maacathite, and all Mount Hermon, and all the Bashan as far as Salecah;
pieces: and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah,

L.11: and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah,

R.11: It took in Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah.

decisions.choice: Gilead, Bashan, Salecah: the hill country and the high plains east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead is the hill country east of the Jordan on both sides of the Jabbok. Bashan is the fertile plain to its north and east, toward Mount Hermon. Salecah was on the far eastern edge of Bashan (Deuteronomy 3:10).

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: two small kingdoms north-east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: These peoples lived between Bashan and Mount Hermon, east of the Sea of Chinnereth (Deuteronomy 3:14; 2 Samuel 3:3; 10:6). They are not the southern Geshurites of verse 2.

records.source: כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וּת עוֹג֙ בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁר־מָלַ֥ךְ בְּעַשְׁתָּר֖וֹת וּבְאֶדְרֶ֑עִי ה֤וּא נִשְׁאַר֙ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָרְפָאִ֔ים וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּרִשֵֽׁם׃
records.gloss: all [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei; he was left of [the] remnant of the Rephaim; and struck them Moses and dispossessed them.
pieces: the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last survivors of the Rephaim. Moses defeated them and drove them out.

L.12: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei. He was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. And Moses struck them and dispossessed them.

R.12: It took in the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim, a people remembered as giants. Moses defeated these kings and drove out their people.

decisions.choice: Og, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei: the second king defeated under Moses
decisions.reason: Og king of Bashan came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated (Numbers 21:33-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-11). Ashtaroth and Edrei were his royal cities (12:4).

decisions.choice: the remnant of the Rephaim: an older people known for their size
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an ancient people of the land, remembered as very tall (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21). Og is called the last of them, and his great iron bed was still shown in Rabbah (Deuteronomy 3:11).

decisions.choice: them: Sihon and Og with their peoples
decisions.reason: "Them" goes back over verses 10-12 to the two kings and the peoples of their kingdoms. Moses defeated both and Israel took their land.

decisions.choice: a people remembered as giants; these kings and ... their people
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Rephaim were, as m2 does, and says who "them" are.

pieces: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did not drive out the Geshurites and the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.

L.13: But the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live in the midst of Israel to this day.

R.13: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did not drive out the people of Geshur and Maacath. They still live among the Israelites today.

decisions.choice: did not dispossess: a task left undone
decisions.reason: The book notes several peoples that Israel did not drive out (15:63; 16:10; 17:12-13). Here it is the two small kingdoms of verse 11. Later David married a daughter of the king of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:3).

decisions.choice: Geshur and Maacath: the two peoples named by their lands
decisions.reason: The names of the lands stand for their peoples. "Maacath" is the form used here for the land elsewhere called Maacah (2 Samuel 10:6).

decisions.choice: to this day: to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The writer speaks from a later time and notes that the situation still holds (as in 4:9; 5:9).

decisions.choice: dispossess (Literal) / drive out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.gloss: Only to [the] tribe of the Levi not he gave an inheritance; [the] offerings by fire of Yahweh, God of Israel, it [is] his inheritance, just as he spoke to him.
pieces: Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The food offerings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised it.

L.14: Only to the tribe of Levi he did not give an inheritance; the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to it.

R.14: But Moses gave no land to the tribe of Levi. Instead, the food offerings burned for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are their share, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

decisions.choice: he did not give: Moses
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but it is Moses, who gave the eastern lands (verses 8 and 15), as verse 33 says outright.

decisions.choice: no inheritance for Levi: the tribe received towns, not a territory
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi served at the sanctuary and received no share of the land. It was given towns to live in, with pasture around them (chapter 21; Numbers 35:1-8).

decisions.choice: the offerings by fire of the LORD: the gifts brought to the LORD at the altar
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 18:1. Parts of many offerings went to the priests and Levites as food, and these, with the tithes, were how the tribe lived (Numbers 18:8-24).

decisions.choice: as he promised it: the LORD's word to Aaron and Levi
decisions.reason: The LORD said that he himself would be Levi's share among Israel (Numbers 18:20; Deuteronomy 10:9; 18:2). "It" and "its" refer to the tribe, which the Hebrew speaks of as one person ("him", "his").

decisions.choice: offerings by fire (Literal) / food offerings (Balanced) / food offerings burned (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 18:1.

decisions.choice: Moses; their; them
decisions.reason: Readable names Moses as the one who gave the land, and speaks of the tribe as "they", which is more natural in English than "it".

records.gloss: And gave Moses to [the] tribe of [the] sons of Reuben according to their clans.
pieces: Moses gave land to the tribe of the descendants of Reuben, clan by clan.

L.15: And Moses gave to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans.

R.15: Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben, family by family.

decisions.choice: Moses gave: what he gave is told in what follows
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no object; the next verses spell out the land given. This begins the list of the three eastern shares: Reuben (verses 15-23), Gad (24-28) and the half-tribe of Manasseh (29-31).

decisions.choice: according to their clans: shared out among the clans of the tribe
decisions.reason: The clan was the group of families within a tribe. Each tribe's land was divided among its clans (Numbers 26:5-7, 52-56).

decisions.choice: gave land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "land" as the object of "gave".

records.heading: The land of Reuben

R.16: Their land reached from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River valley, and took in the town in the middle of the valley and all the high plain around Medeba.

decisions.choice: Aroer, the city in the wadi, the plateau: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The southern part of the eastern lands, described in verse 9, goes to Reuben. Reuben's land lay north of the Arnon and east of the Dead Sea.

records.gloss: Heshbon and all its cities which [are] on the plateau: Dibon and Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,
pieces: Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,

L.17: Heshbon and all its cities that are on the plateau: Dibon and Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,

R.17: It included Heshbon and all the towns around it on the high plain: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,

decisions.choice: Heshbon and all its cities: Sihon's capital and the towns that belonged to it
decisions.reason: Heshbon had been Sihon's royal city (verse 10; Numbers 21:25-26). Its "cities" are the towns of the plateau around it. In Numbers 32:37 Heshbon is rebuilt by Reuben; in 21:39 it is a town of the Levites in the land of Gad, so it may have lain on the border.

decisions.choice: Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon: names that recall the god Baal
decisions.reason: Bamoth-baal means "high places of Baal" (Numbers 22:41), and Beth-baal-meon "house of Baal of Meon", the town called Baal-meon in Numbers 32:38. The names are kept as they stand.

records.source: וְיַ֥הְצָה וּקְדֵמֹ֖ת וּמֵפָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: and Jahaz and Kedemoth and Mephaath,
pieces: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

L.18: and Jahaz and Kedemoth and Mephaath,

decisions.choice: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath: towns on the eastern plateau
decisions.reason: Jahaz is where Israel defeated Sihon (Numbers 21:23). Kedemoth lay near the eastern desert (Deuteronomy 2:26). Jahaz, Kedemoth and Mephaath later became towns of the Levites (21:36-37).

pieces: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,

L.19: and Kiriathaim and Sibmah and Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,

R.19: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,

decisions.choice: the hill of the valley: high ground above the Jordan valley or the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The "valley" is probably the deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, as in verse 27. Zereth-shahar, "the glow of dawn", stood on a height above it.

decisions.choice: Kiriathaim, Sibmah: towns of the plateau
decisions.reason: Both are named among the towns Reuben rebuilt (Numbers 32:37-38); Sibmah was later known for its vines (Isaiah 16:8-9).

L.20: and Beth-peor and the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

R.20: Beth-peor, the slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth.

decisions.choice: Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth-jeshimoth: the land facing Jericho
decisions.reason: These places lay at the north-east end of the Dead Sea, where Israel camped before crossing (Numbers 33:49). Pisgah is the height from which Moses saw the land, and Moses was buried in the valley near Beth-peor (Deuteronomy 34:1, 6).

decisions.choice: Mount Pisgah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Mount" so the reader knows Pisgah is a mountain.

records.gloss: and all [the] cities of the plateau, and all [the] kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorite, who reigned in Heshbon, whom struck Moses, him and [the] leaders of Midian, Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, princes of Sihon, dwellers of the land.
pieces: all the towns of the plateau, and the whole kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses had defeated him and the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes allied with Sihon who lived in the land.

L.21: and all the cities of the plateau, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, him and the leaders of Midian, Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, dwelling in the land.

R.21: It took in all the towns of the high plain and the whole kingdom of Sihon, the Amorite king who had ruled from Heshbon. Moses had defeated him. He had also defeated the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba. They were rulers under Sihon who lived in that land.

decisions.choice: the leaders of Midian: the five Midianite kings of Numbers 31:8
decisions.reason: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba are named as the five kings of Midian killed in Israel's war against Midian (Numbers 31:8), after Midian led Israel into sin at Peor (Numbers 25).

decisions.choice: princes of Sihon: rulers bound to Sihon
decisions.reason: The word is used of princes or chiefs and may come from a root linked with pouring out an offering when a ruler was installed. Here it seems to mean that these Midianite chiefs were under Sihon's rule or allied with him, so their defeat belongs to the account of his kingdom.

decisions.choice: leaders: the heads of the Midianite peoples
decisions.reason: The same word names the leaders of Israel's tribes. In Numbers 31:8 the same men are called "kings".

decisions.choice: the princes allied with Sihon
decisions.reason: Balanced says "allied with" for the bare "of Sihon", following m2. Readable says "rulers under Sihon".

decisions.choice: Moses had defeated him ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence at "whom Moses struck" to end the long list.

records.gloss: And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, killed [the] sons of Israel with the sword among their slain.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} also killed Balaam son of Beor, who practiced divination, with the sword, along with the others they killed.

L.22: And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel killed with the sword among their slain.

R.22: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword, together with the others they killed. He was a man who claimed to tell the future by reading signs.

decisions.choice: Balaam son of Beor killed: as told in Numbers 31:8
decisions.reason: Balaam had been hired to curse Israel but blessed them (Numbers 22-24). He later advised Midian to draw Israel into sin at Peor (Numbers 31:16), and he died with the kings of Midian in Israel's war against them (Numbers 31:8).

decisions.choice: the diviner: one who sought omens and signs
decisions.reason: The word names the practice of reading signs to learn the future or the will of the gods, which the law forbids in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10). Joshua calls Balaam by this title rather than "prophet".

decisions.choice: among their slain: along with the others they killed
decisions.reason: Balaam is named apart from the five kings, but he fell in the same battle, among those Israel killed.

decisions.choice: Balaam is named first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Balaam before the verb to set him apart in the account.

decisions.choice: a man who claimed to tell the future by reading signs
decisions.reason: Readable explains "diviner" in a sentence of its own.

records.gloss: And was [the] border of [the] sons of Reuben the Jordan and [its] border. This [is the] inheritance of [the] sons of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
pieces: The Jordan and its banks formed the border of the Reubenites. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Reuben, clan by clan, the towns and their villages.

L.23: And the border of the sons of Reuben was the Jordan and [its] border. This was the inheritance of the sons of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

R.23: The Jordan River was the western border of Reuben's land. This was the land the families of the tribe of Reuben received, the towns and their villages.

decisions.choice: the Jordan and its border: the river with the land along it formed the boundary
decisions.reason: The phrase means the river served as the border, with the strip of land on its bank. The same wording is used for Gad in verse 27 and in Numbers 34:6 for the sea.

decisions.choice: their villages: the open settlements around each town
decisions.reason: The word names small settlements without walls, the farming villages that belonged to a walled town and lay in its fields (Leviticus 25:31).

decisions.choice: this was the inheritance: a closing formula
decisions.reason: Each tribe's share ends with this summary, as for Gad in verse 28 and throughout chapters 15-19.

decisions.choice: the western border
decisions.reason: Readable adds "western", since the Jordan ran along the west of Reuben's land.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן מֹשֶׁה֙ לְמַטֵּה־גָ֔ד לִבְנֵי־גָ֖ד לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And gave Moses to [the] tribe of Gad, to [the] sons of Gad, according to their clans.
pieces: Moses gave land to the tribe of Gad, to the descendants of Gad, clan by clan.

L.24: And Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad, according to their clans.

R.24: Moses gave land to the tribe of Gad, family by family.

decisions.choice: Moses gave to the tribe of Gad: the second eastern share
decisions.reason: As in verse 15 for Reuben. Gad's land lay north of Reuben's, in the Jordan valley and the hills of Gilead (Numbers 32:34-36).

decisions.choice: gave land
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

records.heading: The land of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh

pieces: Their territory was Jazer and all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, up to Aroer east of Rabbah,

L.25: And their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah,

R.25: Their land took in Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half of the land that had belonged to the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, east of Rabbah.

decisions.choice: half the land of the sons of Ammon: land once Ammonite, taken earlier by Sihon
decisions.reason: Israel was not to take the Ammonites' own land (Deuteronomy 2:19, 37). This part had been Ammonite but was in Sihon's hands when Israel defeated him, so it came to Gad (Judges 11:13-22).

decisions.choice: Aroer east of Rabbah: another Aroer, near the Ammonite capital
decisions.reason: This is not the Aroer on the Arnon (verse 16). Rabbah was the Ammonite capital, modern Amman. "On the face of" here means facing it, most likely to the east; the exact place of this Aroer is not known.

decisions.choice: the land that had belonged to the Ammonites
decisions.reason: Readable says "had belonged", following m1: the land was no longer Ammonite.

records.source: וּמֵחֶשְׁבּ֛וֹן עַד־רָמַ֥ת הַמִּצְפֶּ֖ה וּבְטֹנִ֑ים וּמִֽמַּחֲנַ֖יִם עַד־גְּב֥וּל לִדְבִֽר׃
records.gloss: and from Heshbon as far as Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim as far as [the] border of Debir;
pieces: and from Heshbon up to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim up to the border of Debir,

L.26: and from Heshbon as far as Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim as far as the border of Debir,

R.26: It went from Heshbon up to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim up to the border of Debir.

decisions.choice: from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim; from Mahanaim: Gad's southern and northern limits
decisions.reason: The first line runs north from Heshbon on the plateau. Mahanaim, the place where Jacob saw the angels of God (Genesis 32:3), lay near the Jabbok and marked the line between Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh (verse 30).

decisions.choice: Debir: a town in Gilead, not the Debir of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read as the name Lidebir, or as "to Debir". The town may be Lo-debar in Gilead (2 Samuel 9:4; Amos 6:13). It is not the Debir west of the Jordan (10:38; 15:15).

records.source: וּבָעֵ֡מֶק בֵּ֣ית הָרָם֩ וּבֵ֨ית נִמְרָ֜ה וְסֻכּ֣וֹת וְצָפ֗וֹן יֶ֚תֶר מַמְלְכ֗וּת סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וּגְבֻ֑ל עַד־קְצֵה֙ יָם־כִּנֶּ֔רֶת עֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מִזְרָֽחָה׃
records.gloss: and in the valley: Beth-haram and Beth-nimrah and Succoth and Zaphon, [the] rest of [the] kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and [its] border, as far as [the] end of [the] Sea of Chinnereth, across the Jordan eastward.
pieces: and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, what remained of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan as its border up to the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the east side of the Jordan.

L.27: and in the valley, Beth-haram and Beth-nimrah and Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and [its] border, as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, across the Jordan eastward.

R.27: In the Jordan valley it took in Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, which were what was left of the kingdom of Sihon, the king who ruled from Heshbon. The Jordan was its western border, up to the south end of the Sea of Chinnereth (Lake Galilee), on the east side of the river.

decisions.choice: the valley: the Jordan valley east of the river
decisions.reason: The valley is the low land along the east bank of the Jordan, from near the Dead Sea north toward the Sea of Chinnereth. Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon were towns in it (Numbers 32:36; Genesis 33:17).

decisions.choice: as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth: its southern tip
decisions.reason: The Sea of Chinnereth is the lake later called the Sea of Galilee. Gad's land along the Jordan reached up to its southern end.

decisions.choice: the Jordan and its border: as in verse 23
decisions.reason: The river formed the boundary, here the western edge of Gad's land in the valley.

decisions.choice: the Jordan valley; western border; south end; (Lake Galilee)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain which valley is meant, that the river was the border on the west, that the land reached the south end of the lake, and gives the lake's later name, following the meaning decisions.

records.source: זֹ֛את נַחֲלַ֥ת בְּנֵי־גָ֖ד לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם הֶעָרִ֖ים וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: This [is the] inheritance of [the] sons of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
pieces: This was the inheritance of the descendants of Gad, clan by clan, the towns and their villages.

L.28: This was the inheritance of the sons of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

R.28: This was the land the families of the tribe of Gad received, the towns and their villages.

decisions.choice: this was the inheritance: the closing formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה לַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיְהִ֗י לַחֲצִ֛י מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And gave Moses to half [the] tribe of Manasseh; and it was for half [the] tribe of [the] sons of Manasseh according to their clans.
pieces: Moses gave land to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It belonged to half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, clan by clan.

L.29: And Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; and it was for the half-tribe of the sons of Manasseh according to their clans.

R.29: Moses gave land to half of the tribe of Manasseh, family by family.

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh: the eastern part of the tribe
decisions.reason: The clans of Machir and Jair, who had taken Gilead and Bashan (Numbers 32:39-42), settled east of the Jordan. The rest of Manasseh received land west of the river (17:1-13).

decisions.choice: and it was for: the land is said to belong to the half-tribe
decisions.reason: The second clause repeats the first in other words, making plain that the gift was for the clans of that half of the tribe only.

decisions.choice: gave land
decisions.reason: As in verse 15. Readable joins the two clauses, which say the same thing.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י גְבוּלָ֗ם מִמַּחֲנַ֨יִם כָּֽל־הַבָּשָׁ֜ן כָּֽל־מַמְלְכ֣וּת׀ע֣וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֗ן וְכָל־חַוֺּ֥ת יָאִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן שִׁשִּׁ֥ים עִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And was their territory from Mahanaim, all the Bashan, all [the] kingdom of Og king of the Bashan, and all [the] villages of Jair which [are] in the Bashan, sixty cities;
pieces: Their territory reached from Mahanaim through all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, with all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns,

L.30: And their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities,

R.30: Their land reached from Mahanaim and took in all of Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og, king of Bashan. It took in all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns.

decisions.choice: the villages of Jair: the settlements called Havvoth-jair
decisions.reason: Jair, of the tribe of Manasseh, took these settlements and named them after himself (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14). The word may first have meant tent camps; here it names towns.

decisions.choice: sixty cities: the towns of the region of Argob
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 3:4-5 counts sixty walled towns in the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan, besides many open villages.

records.source: וַחֲצִ֤י הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְעַשְׁתָּר֣וֹת וְאֶדְרֶ֔עִי עָרֵ֛י מַמְלְכ֥וּת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָׁ֑ן לִבְנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לַחֲצִ֥י בְנֵֽי־מָכִ֖יר לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: and half the Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan, [were] for [the] sons of Machir son of Manasseh, for half [of the] sons of Machir, according to their clans.
pieces: and half of Gilead, with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal towns of Og in Bashan. These were given to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the descendants of Machir, clan by clan.

L.31: and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the sons of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the sons of Machir, according to their clans.

R.31: It also took in half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns where Og had ruled in Bashan. This land went to the families of Machir's descendants who lived east of the Jordan. Machir was the son of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: Machir son of Manasseh: the main clan of the tribe
decisions.reason: Machir was Manasseh's firstborn (17:1). His descendants took Gilead from the Amorites, and Moses gave it to them (Numbers 32:39-40).

decisions.choice: half of the sons of Machir: the part of Machir's line that settled in the east
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the eastern half of the tribe apart from the western half, which also traced its line through Machir (17:1-3).

decisions.choice: half of Gilead: the northern half, beyond the Jabbok
decisions.reason: Gilead was shared: the southern half went to Gad (verse 25) and the northern half, toward Bashan, to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deuteronomy 3:12-13).

decisions.choice: the families of Machir's descendants who lived east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable says what "half of the sons of Machir" means, following m2, and gives Machir's father in a sentence of its own.

records.source: אֵ֕לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־נִחַ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת מוֹאָ֑ב מֵעֵ֛בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרִיח֖וֹ מִזְרָֽחָה׃ס
records.gloss: These [are what] gave as inheritance Moses in [the] plains of Moab, across [the] Jordan [of] Jericho eastward.
pieces: These are the inheritances Moses gave out in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho, to the east.

L.32: These are what Moses gave as inheritances in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan of Jericho eastward.

R.32: This is how Moses divided the land among these tribes while Israel was camped in the plains of Moab, on the east side of the Jordan, across from Jericho.

decisions.choice: the plains of Moab: Israel's last camp before the crossing
decisions.reason: The plains of Moab are the low, open land north-east of the Dead Sea, where Israel camped while Moses gave his last laws (Numbers 22:1; 36:13).

decisions.choice: the Jordan of Jericho: the stretch of the river by Jericho
decisions.reason: The phrase names the part of the Jordan near Jericho, as in Numbers 22:1. The plains lay on the far side of it, facing the city.

decisions.choice: gave as inheritances: shared out as lasting family land
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word "inheritance" and means to give land to be held by a family for good.

decisions.choice: while Israel was camped in
decisions.reason: Readable says why the plains of Moab are named: it was the place of Israel's camp.

records.source: וּלְשֵׁ֨בֶט֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י לֹֽא־נָתַ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה נַחֲלָ֑ה יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: But to [the] tribe of the Levi not gave Moses an inheritance; Yahweh, God of Israel, he [is] their inheritance, just as he spoke to them.
pieces: But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

L.33: But to the tribe of Levi Moses did not give an inheritance; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is their inheritance, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them.

R.33: But Moses gave no land to the tribe of Levi. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, is their share, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

decisions.choice: the LORD is their inheritance: the LORD himself takes the place of land
decisions.reason: Verse 14 said Levi lives on the offerings; here the same truth is said in the deepest way: the LORD himself is the tribe's share. Their life is to serve him and be cared for from what is given to him (Numbers 18:20; Deuteronomy 10:9).

decisions.choice: as he promised them: Numbers 18:20 and Deuteronomy 18:2
decisions.reason: As in verse 14. The verse closes the account of the eastern lands by repeating verse 14, and so frames verses 15-32.

decisions.choice: he is their inheritance: the pronoun stresses the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "he" after naming the LORD, to point to him as the share.

decisions.choice: is their inheritance (no repeated pronoun)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the repeated "he", which English does not need after the name. Readable says "share" for "inheritance".
